items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: thing to honor women — Nancy Wilson, Clora Bryant, Jane Jarvis, Diva

ctx.x: It’s a history of the womens’ swing bands from the 30s and 40s. I’ve never read a better researched book in my life. It’s horrifying actually how women are left out of history. I mean I’ve cited this example to a million people but there was a band called the Darlings of Rhythm, this is from Sherrie’s book, that played at the Apollo Theatre more than any other band, and it was either 1944 or 1946. And in the book, The History of the Apollo, they’re not even mentioned once as even having ever played there. Just as…

thing to honor women — Nancy Wilson, Clora Bryant, Jane Jarvis, Diva, and we were sponsored by a Vodka company called Gray Goose Vodka. So we did this charity event for “Dress for Success” and Clora Bryant came, she’s a trumpet player from Los Angeles. Do you know her well?
No I don’t know her well but I know the name.
